investigation.title: Remote Agent Pod Scheduling Failure: Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity Across All 6 Nodes
investigation.summary: All three remote-agents eval checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api because every pod submitted for remote agent creation was rejected as Unschedulable: 2 nodes reported Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity and the remaining 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity/selector. No evidence (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) was collected because the pod never left the pending state, meaning the agent VM was never provisioned.
investigation.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the remote-agents feature has exhausted its schedulable kata.peerpods.io/vm resource slots. Of the 6 available nodes, 2 carry the kata peer-pods label but both report insufficient remaining VM capacity, and the other 4 do not satisfy the pod's node affinity/selector at all. Preemption cannot help because no lower-priority victims exist on the 2 eligible nodes. As a result, every remote-agent pod is stuck Unschedulable and no agent VM is ever assigned, so the eval probe never receives a vmId or remoteState and all required evidence fields remain empty. This is an eval-detected infrastructure capacity constraint, not a confirmed user-traffic outage; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence.

investigations.title: Remote Agent Pod Scheduling Failure: Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity Across All 6 Nodes
investigations.summary: All three remote-agents eval checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api because every pod submitted for remote agent creation was rejected as Unschedulable: 2 nodes reported Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity and the remaining 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity/selector. No evidence (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) was collected because the pod never left the pending state, meaning the agent VM was never provisioned.
investigations.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the remote-agents feature has exhausted its schedulable kata.peerpods.io/vm resource slots. Of the 6 available nodes, 2 carry the kata peer-pods label but both report insufficient remaining VM capacity, and the other 4 do not satisfy the pod's node affinity/selector at all. Preemption cannot help because no lower-priority victims exist on the 2 eligible nodes. As a result, every remote-agent pod is stuck Unschedulable and no agent VM is ever assigned, so the eval probe never receives a vmId or remoteState and all required evidence fields remain empty. This is an eval-detected infrastructure capacity constraint, not a confirmed user-traffic outage; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence.

whatWouldDisproveThis: If the GitHub Actions workflow run history shows a successful snapshot-publishing run completed within the last 300 minutes prior to 2026-06-19T05:33:10Z, the workflow-skipped hypothesis would be disproved and the cause would shift to a CDN caching or deployment propagation delay.

If the snapshot's generatedAt timestamp is within 300 minutes of the eval run time but snapshotAgeMinutes is computed incorrectly by the runner, the staleness would be a measurement error in infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs rather than a true publication gap.

If the staleAfterMinutes=360 registry value is intentional and the workflow runs on a 360-minute cadence, and the eval contract's maxAgeMinutes=300 is a misconfiguration (should be >= 360), then the root cause would be a contract/config misalignment rather than a missed workflow run.

If a subsequent eval run immediately after this one shows snapshotAgeMinutes <= 300 without any workflow intervention, the failure would indicate a transient timing race between the workflow publish step and the eval probe, not a sustained workflow outage.
followUpEvals: Add an eval that directly checks the GitHub Actions workflow run recency for the snapshot-publishing job, asserting that the last successful run completed within the last 300 minutes. This would catch a missed workflow run before the snapshot itself becomes stale.

Add a separate eval assertion that validates the relationship between staleAfterMinutes (registry) and maxAgeMinutes (contract) to detect configuration drift between these two values before it causes recurring eval failures.
Add a trend eval that tracks snapshotAgeMinutes over consecutive runs to detect a gradual drift toward the 300-minute ceiling, enabling early warning before the threshold is breached.
